### (a) Thermal Bridge Surcharges and Linear \\(\Psi\\)-Values in Swiss Proofs

* **SIA 380/1 Limit Values (\\(\Psi\\)-limits) for New Construction Details**:
  * **Source Title**: *Checkliste Wärmebrücken Neubau Version 10.0* (Konferenz Kantonaler Energiefachstellen EnFK / EnDK) [1]
  * **Section / Page**: Pages 4, 6, 8, 12–15 [2-5]
  * **Building Type**: Residential buildings (single-family and multi-family / *Wohnbauten*) [1]
  * **Year of Data**: 2023 (valid through 31.12.2026) [2]
  * **Values**:
    * **1.1 Balkonplatte (Balcony slab):** Limit **\\(\Psi \le 0.30 \text{ W/mK}\\)** [2]
    * **2.1 Geschossdecke / Soletta (Floor slab):** Limit **\\(\Psi \le 0.20 \text{ W/mK}\\)** [6]
    * **2.2 Wandanschluss an Kellerdecke (Wall connection to cellar ceiling):** Limit **\\(\Psi \le 0.20 \text{ W/mK}\\)** (example construction details range from \\(0.35 \text{ to } 0.80 \text{ W/mK}\\)) [3, 7]
    * **3.4 Sockeldetail (Cellar base detail, unheated or heated cellar):** Limit **\\(\Psi \le 0.20 \text{ W/mK}\\)** [4, 8, 9]
    * **5.1–5.3 Fensteranschlag (Window reveal / sill / lintel):** Limit **\\(\Psi \le 0.15 \text{ W/mK}\\)** (example construction details range from \\(0.08 \text{ to } 0.20 \text{ W/mK}\\)) [5, 10]

* **Default Thermal Bridge Surcharge (\\(\Delta U_{tb}\\))**:
  * **Source Title**: *TABULA Common Calculation Method* (IWU / TABULA) [11]
  * **Section / Page**: Appendix / Pages 32, 34, 54 [12-14]
  * **Building Type**: Multi-Family House (**MFH** example building) [15]
  * **Year of Data**: 2013 [16]
  * **Values**: Standard default surcharge **\\(\Delta U_{tb} = 0.10 \text{ W/(m²K)}\\)** for original/unrefurbished states; **\\(\Delta U_{tb} = 0.05 \text{ W/(m²K)}\\)** for advanced refurbishment [13, 14].

* **Thermal Bridge Contribution to Heat Load**:
  * **Source Title**: *Schlussbericht: Der Heizleistungsbedarf als Beurteilungsgrösse für die energetische Qualität der Gebäudehülle* (Minergie / EnDK) [17]
  * **Section / Page**: Section 9 & Appendix A4, Pages 23 & 54 [18, 19]
  * **Building Type**: Single-family houses (**EFH**, \\(n = 73\\)) and Multi-family houses (**MFH**, \\(n = 74\\)) [17, 19]
  * **Year of Data**: 2014 [17]
  * **Values**: Thermal bridge losses contribute **\\(0.5 \text{ to } 5 \text{ W/m²}\\)** of floor area to the design heat load (representing **ca. 5% to 20%**, with an average of **~10%** of total design heat load) [18, 19].

---

### (b) Temperature Reduction Factors \\(b\\) for Floors / Cellars (Measured vs. Default)

* **Default Normative \\(b\\)-Factors**:
  * **Source Title**: *The prebound-effect in detail: real indoor temperatures in basements and measured versus calculated U-values* (Caroline Hoffmann & Achim Geissler, FHNW / CISBAT 2017 / Energy Procedia 122 (2017) 32–37) [20]
  * **Section / Page**: Section 2.2 & Section 4.2, Pages 33 & 36 [21-23]
  * **Building Type**: Single-family houses (e.g. Basel 07 built 1928, Münchenstein 01 built 1925) and Multi-family houses (e.g. Basel 08 ~1950, Reinach 01 1962/63) [21, 24]
  * **Year of Data**: 2017 (field measurements from winter 2015/16) [25]
  * **Values**:
    * **SIA 380/1:2015 Default Values:** **\\(b = 0.7\\)** for unheated cellar full-faced to ground; **\\(b = 0.8\\)** for cellar partly faced to ground [22, 23].
    * **Calculated Normative \\(b\\)-factor (SN EN ISO 13789):** **\\(b = 0.78\\)** for an unheated basement (yielding a calculated basement temperature of \\(8.3^\circ\text{C}\\) at an outdoor mean of \\(5.1^\circ\text{C}\\)) [22, 23].
    * **TABULA Default:** **\\(b_{tr} = 0.5\\)** for unheated cellars and soil (*TABULA Common Calculation Method*, 2013, Table 2, p. 11) [26].

* **Measured \\(b\\)-Factors & Real Basement Temperatures**:
  * **Source Title**: *The prebound-effect in detail: real indoor temperatures in basements and measured versus calculated U-values* (Hoffmann & Geissler, FHNW, 2017) [20]
  * **Section / Page**: Section 3.2, 4.2 & 5, Pages 34–37 [22, 27, 28]
  * **Building Type**: Single-family houses and Multi-family houses [21, 24]
  * **Year of Data**: 2017 (winter 2015/16 measurements) [25]
  * **Values**:
    * **Measured unheated basement temperatures:** Ranged between **\\(13^\circ\text{C} \text{ and } 21^\circ\text{C}\\)** across six measured basements (averaging **~8 K higher** than normative calculation methods yielding \\(8.3^\circ\text{C}\\)) [27, 29-31].
    * **Derived Measured \\(b\\)-factor:** Based on the lowest measured basement temperature of \\(13^\circ\text{C}\\), the iterative \\(b\\)-factor is **0.51** (authors recommend using **\\(b = 0.5\\)** for existing buildings with uninsulated cellar ceilings when balancing demand and consumption) [22, 23, 28, 32].

---

### (c) Minimum Air Change Rate for Design Heat Load

* **Status in Sources**: **not in the sources**. The specific numerical minimum air change rate for design heat load calculation (e.g., under EN 12831 / SIA 384.201) is not provided in the uploaded source excerpts (the excerpt for `prEN 12831-1:2025` lists table of contents headings Annex A.3.4 / B.3.4 "Air change rate", but does not contain the numerical values) [33, 34].

* **Related Ventilation Figures Available in Sources**:
  * **TABULA Standard Calculation**: Utilisation air change \\(n_{\text{use}} = 0.4 \text{ h}^{-1}\\), infiltration air change \\(n_{\text{infilt}} = 0.2 \text{ h}^{-1}\\) (total \\(n = 0.6 \text{ h}^{-1}\\)) (*TABULA Common Calculation Method*, 2013, Table 1, p. 9) [11, 13, 35].
  * **SIA Standard Usage Air Flow**: In *Harmonisierung SIA-Standardwerte* (`cms.sia.ch/getMedia/941`, 2019, Table 14, p. 25), SIA 2024:2015 specifies **\\(36 \text{ m³/h per person}\\)** (\\(1.00 \text{ W/m²}\\) for EFH, \\(0.60 \text{ W/m²}\\) for MFH), updated in prSIA 2024:2021 to **\\(29 \text{ m³/h per person}\\)** (\\(0.83 \text{ W/m²}\\) for EFH, \\(0.58 \text{ W/m²}\\) for MFH) [36].

---

CISBAT 2017 International Conference – Future Buildings & Districts – Energy Efficiency from Nano to Urban Scale, CISBAT 2017 6-8 September 2017, Lausanne, Switzerland The prebound-effect in detail: real indoor temperatures in basements and measured versus calculated U-values  Caroline Hoffmanna*, Achim Geisslera aIntitut Energie am Bau, Fachhochschule Nordwestschweiz, St. Jakob-Strasse 84, 4132 Muttenz, Switzerland  Abstract This paper focuses on the topics U-values and indoor air temperatures of unheated basements with uninsulated cellar ceilings. Measurement values are compared with calculation procedures suggested by building regulations. Concerning the U-values it is shown that they are typically considered to be higher (i.e. worse) in uninsulated existing constructions than they effectively are. Measured temperatures in seven basements are higher (around 8 K) than a calculation according to regulations would yield. The paper derives suggestions for the adjustment of calculations focused on existing residential buildings.  © 2017 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. For an exemplary basement, the temperatures and the corresponding b-factor (for the ceiling) are calculated according to SN EN ISO 13789 (see equations (2) and (3)). The following boundary conditions apply for the calculation: The basement floor is 2 m below ground level and is uninsulated. Construction U-values are: wall facing exterior 0.9 W/(m2 K), wall facing ground 0.5 W/(m2 K) and basement floor 1.0 W/(m2 K)). The U-values for the components adjoining ground are adjusted by the appropriate b-factors. The ground floor above the basement is conditioned (walls: 0.55 W/(m2 K), floor 0.8 W/(m2

For the basement used as example, the calculated b-value is 0.78, the corresponding temperature is 8.3 °C (boundary condition: normative outdoor temperature for Basel-Binningen, mean of the heating period 5.1 °C Oct-6 Caroline Hoffmann and Achim Geissler / Energy Procedia 00 (2017) 000–000 Mar). The calculated b-factor is close to the default values proposed by SIA 380/1:2015 for unheated cellars (0.7 cellar full-faced to ground, 0.8 cellar partly faced to ground).  In order to find out which b-factor corresponds to the lowest measured temperature of 13°C an iterative approach based on the procedure according to [4] is necessary. The corresponding b-factor found is 0.51.

The measurement does not take this into account. 3.2. Temperatures of basements with uninsulated cellar ceiling The basement temperatures are found to be between a minimum of 13 °C and a maximum of 21 °C (Fig. 1 (b)). The outdoor temperatures during these periods were between -0.8 and 13.8 °C on a weekly average. Overall, the measurement results are between 2.3 and 5 K apart from each other. Omitting one building with exceptionally high temperatures (Reinach 01) the difference would be 0.5 to 2.5 K. Summarising all measurements, the minimal basement temperature is 13 °C. Basement temperatures calculated according to EN ISO 13789 are found to be significantly lower, namely on average by 7.3 K (omitting Reinach 01 and 2  = 3 K).

Temperature measurements in basements of existing buildings reveal considerably higher values (around 8 K) than a calculation according to applicable building codes would yield. Especially when the cellar ceiling is uninsulated the indoor air temperature assumed for the cellar determines the calculated heat loss of this component. Therefore, it is necessary to use reasonable cellar temperatures when demand / consumption alignment is of interest. We suggest the use of a b-factor of 0.5 for existing buildings with uninsulated cellar ceilings.
